text:
Nothing to ask first. Switching channels doesn't spend money, touch a repo, or put a token on a device, and passwordless sudo works here.

Check what the switch would do first:

```sh
tentmaker version --json
sudo tentmaker update --channel dev --check --json
```

Then switch:

```sh
sudo tentmaker update --channel dev --json
```

The update verifies the sha256, checks that the new binary runs, swaps it in, and restarts the service. It rolls back on its own if the service isn't healthy within 60 seconds. It only updates between jobs, so a running job isn't interrupted.

Verify:

```sh
tentmaker version --json
tentmaker doctor --json
```

The version should look like `0.1.1-dev.<timestamp>.<sha>`, and `doctor` should exit 0.

The docs I have don't say whether `--channel dev` is remembered for future auto-updates (`update.auto` checks every 6 hours). After the switch, I'd run `sudo tentmaker update --check --json` again to see which channel it checks. If it reports stable, I'd look up the channel key in `docs/config.md` and set it with `sudo tentmaker budget set`-style config commands, rather than guess.

If the dev build misbehaves, `sudo tentmaker rollback` returns you to the previous binary. Dev is rebuilt on every push to `main`, so expect more churn than stable.
